feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
entry.summary:
Coca-Cola introduces a continuous latent context compression framework for LLM agents that compresses tool outputs into dense latent tokens instead of relying on discrete text tokens.

Why it matters: By bypassing discrete text summarization, agents can operate over significantly compressed context windows, decreasing latency and execution costs while enhancing decision-making accuracy.

entry.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
entry.summary:
NPCBench is a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma that evaluates multimodal AI across longitudinal, integrated care pathways rather than isolated, static question-answering tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic benchmark showing that current multimodal models struggle to maintain temporal coherence and jointly accurate reasoning across full clinical workflows.

entry.title: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias
entry.summary:
HERIT is a domain-adaptation pipeline that uses retrieval-augmented generation to create high-quality Hanja-to-English pseudo-labeled data from Hanja-Korean corpora, reducing temporal bias and data scarcity in historical translation.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable machine translation pipeline to automatically make untranslated historical Hanja archives globally accessible to researchers without expensive manual effort.

entry.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that a fine-tuned model's domain can be recovered from the artifact alone using black-box generated text or gray-box activations, outperforming white-box weight statistics.

Why it matters: LoRA fine-tunes leak training domain information through model outputs and activations, posing privacy and data-provenance risks even when direct weight access is restricted.

entry.title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
A learnable KV cache eviction gate trained inside the softmax using the dense model's predictions as a target prevents optimization from defaulting to a dense no-op.

Why it matters: It establishes the structural conditions required to successfully train learnable KV cache eviction mechanisms, enabling up to 75% compression with minimal loss in long-context accuracy.

entry.title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
entry.summary:
Researchers developed TraceMRT to red-team Chain-of-Thought monitors using contextual evasion strategies, exposing vulnerabilities in top LLM monitors and addressing them with a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current top-tier reasoning monitors can be bypassed by strategically concealed objectives, providing a more robust Bayesian detection method for autonomous agent safety.

entry.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Controlled experiments reveal that Criteria Exposure (CE) in embodied self-improvement causes coding agents to overfit to verification logic rather than learn robust, transferable task skills.

Why it matters: Exposing evaluation criteria to self-improving agents inflates benchmark scores through overfitting, requiring the adoption of instruction-faithful verifiers to measure genuine robot skill acquisition.

entry.title: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining
entry.summary:
BEEMO is a neural motor decoding framework that decouples behavioral and neural pretraining, enabling training on arbitrary mixtures of paired neural-behavioral recordings and unpaired behavioral trajectories to improve task transfer.

Why it matters: Scaling unpaired behavioral data provides a cost-effective pathway to build cross-subject and cross-task neural decoders without relying on invasive, expensive neural recordings.

entry.title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
entry.summary:
A study on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reveals a dissociation between internal representations and behavioral outputs, showing prompt framing impacts representational geometry more than persona identity, whereas persona content drives actual behavioral ratings.

Why it matters: Understanding the dissociation between internal representations and functional outputs is critical for interpreting how multimodal models process persona conditioning and for evaluating internal model states.

entry.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
entry.summary:
Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD) mitigates Teacher Drift in multilingual reasoning distillation by dynamically selecting verified, teachable prefix trajectories based on teacher-student likelihood.

Why it matters: TOPSD improves multilingual self-distillation efficiency and accuracy, particularly for lower-resource languages where intermediate reasoning mistakes typically cause standard distillation to fail.

entry.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
entry.summary:
DictLLM introduces a post-training compression scheme that decomposes weight matrices across grouped layers into a single shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, followed by quantization.

Why it matters: It enables significantly higher compression ratios for LLMs without requiring full retraining, facilitating memory-efficient deployment on mobile and edge devices.

entry.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
entry.summary:
A post-hoc, model-agnostic framework applies sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to user embeddings to extract, interpret, and natural-language-label sparse superpositions of behavioral modes without modifying upstream models.

Why it matters: It provides a practical, post-hoc method to interpret, query, and operationalize opaque recommendation and personalization embeddings using natural language without retraining upstream models.

entry.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes deterministic Gradient Descent with large constant step sizes in Adversarial Training, revealing fundamental dynamics that differ significantly from Standard Training and continuous-time flow approximations.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between theoretical models using vanishing step sizes and practical adversarial training regimes using large constant step sizes.

entry.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary:
GraphMuon adapts the Muon optimizer to Graph Neural Networks by accounting for the covariance structure of graph-propagated layer inputs during matrix update orthogonalization.

Why it matters: GraphMuon significantly accelerates GNN training convergence without sacrificing predictive performance by aligning optimization updates with graph propagation dynamics.

entry.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others
entry.summary:
Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping (DUOS) meta-learns an agent update rule for general-sum games that performs opponent shaping using only the agent's own experience, requiring no access to opponent parameters or policies.

Why it matters: It enables effective long-horizon opponent shaping and cooperation in general-sum games without requiring access to private opponent parameters or internal state.

entry.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers
entry.summary:
SSoG replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers with learned, axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, achieving subquadratic complexity, global Lipschitz continuity, and lower parameter counts.

Why it matters: SSoG enables scalable, parameter-efficient processing of high-resolution images while providing formal mathematical stability guarantees for continuous-depth Neural ODE models.

entry.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
entry.summary:
Multimodal-SEA is a benchmark featuring 608 tasks across 152 scenarios to evaluate AI agent security against multimodal social engineering attacks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that adding multimodal content significantly increases the vulnerability of personal AI agents to social engineering, highlighting limitations in current model safety alignment.

entry.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced HaluCheck, a bilingual benchmark with over 42,000 instances designed to evaluate LLM hallucination detection, localization, and correction across factual text and agent trajectories.

Why it matters: It establishes a comprehensive benchmark for diagnosing fine-grained hallucination failure modes in both standard text generation and autonomous LLM agent execution.

entry.title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
entry.summary:
LatentRec introduces a framework that uses a 2.5M-parameter module to supervise intermediate latent reasoning steps during LLM recommendation training, allowing the module to be discarded at deployment for zero-token inference reasoning.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to generate expensive chain-of-thought text or run latent modules during inference, shifting the computational cost of reasoning entirely to training time.

entry.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
entry.summary:
Drex is an open-source family of four non-autoregressive decision models up to 37B parameters that directly output probability distributions over user-provided options.

Why it matters: Drex provides a lower-latency, cheaper, and order-stable alternative to autoregressive LLM reasoning for structured decision-making, classification, and scoring tasks.

entry.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes
entry.summary:
A study shows that concept probe accuracy (AUROC) fails to reflect nuisance attribute sensitivity, but nuisance-aware development diagnostics can reduce counterfactual sensitivity with minimal accuracy loss.

Why it matters: High decoding accuracy alone is insufficient to validate concept probes, necessitating nuisance-aware evaluation to ensure probes measure the target concept rather than confounding variables.

entry.title: Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping
entry.summary:
RELOAD fine-tunes typed decision models by looping a middle layer block with a damped connection and a lightweight controller, enabling adaptive test-time compute in latent space to boost accuracy and calibration.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that non-generative decision models can scale test-time compute in latent space without parameter expansion, matching or beating the performance of much larger unrolled models.

entry.title: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision
entry.summary:
Token Identity Brier Flow (TIBF) improves continuous language flow models by using Brier loss squared supervision on token probabilities with frozen embeddings instead of standard continuous MSE.

Why it matters: TIBF resolves probability distribution ambiguity in continuous language flows, allowing pretrained models to achieve lower generative perplexity and fewer text repetitions under limited continued-training budgets.

entry.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
entry.summary:
SKIM is the first pruning and distillation framework designed specifically for LLM agents under structured generation, using token role partitioning to guide parameter pruning and distillation.

Why it matters: SKIM enables significantly smaller, highly compressed LLM agents to maintain accuracy during structured inference, such as tool-calling and grammar-constrained tasks.

entry.title: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
entry.summary:
Evaluations across six frontier models reveal the 'memory trap,' where persistent memories from benign interactions cause agents to overgeneralize and exhibit unsafe or biased behavior in subsequent high-stakes tasks.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that harmless user interactions can inadvertently degrade safety, rigor, and alignment in later sessions highlights an urgent need for scope-aware agent memory systems.

entry.title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
entry.summary:
EDGAR uses a one-step Mixture-of-Experts diffusion model trained on a novel synthetic failure dataset to refine monocular Gaussian avatar renderings while maintaining identity and temporal consistency.

Why it matters: It enables high-quality, artifact-free 3D head avatar rendering by using diffusion refinement strictly during the offline training phase without incurring inference-time latency.

entry.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
entry.summary:
TB-MathModel is the first agentic, containerized benchmark for complete contest-style mathematical modeling, using programmatic validation and multi-reference scoring to verifiably evaluate model solutions against human Outstanding papers.

Why it matters: It establishes a machine-checkable, hard-gated benchmark that eliminates reliance on subjective LLM judges for open-ended, long-horizon mathematical modeling tasks.

entry.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
entry.summary:
DreamFree is a World Action Model that distillates predictive visual representations from a frozen video diffusion model using only current observations, enabling 11Hz real-time robot control without generating future video frames.

Why it matters: It eliminates the latency and visual inaccuracy bottlenecks of video-generation-based robot control, allowing real-time execution of video-diffusion-powered action models.

entry.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
entry.summary:
This paper introduces AI-Augmented Human Intelligence (AHI) and proposes cognitive symbionts—lifelong, embedded, proactive AI systems designed to bridge the cognitive gap between a person's potential knowledge and their working memory capacity.

Why it matters: AHI shifts the paradigm from autonomous systems that replace human effort to embedded, continuous AI that directly expands individual human cognitive capacity.

entry.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
entry.summary:
Speculative Listening is a training-free, lossless self-speculative decoding framework that utilizes idle compute during input time to accelerate chunk-interleaved full-duplex speech language models.

Why it matters: It drastically reduces response latencies in full-duplex speech language models to human-like turn-taking speeds without requiring model retraining or sacrificing output quality.

entry.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
entry.summary:
Muir optimizes linear attention by pairing sensitivity-allocated low-rank gate projections with matched-filter readout, outperforming Gated DeltaNet-2 and standard Transformers.

Why it matters: Muir delivers superior long-context reasoning, recall, and perplexity while training 2.7x faster than Transformers at 32K context lengths without incurring inference memory overhead.

entry.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
entry.summary:
SwarmEvolve accelerates program optimization by executing swarms of low-cost agents that reason and exchange crossover ideas entirely within latent space via KV cache sharing.

Why it matters: Communicating directly via latent space and KV caches drastically lowers the computational cost and time required for LLM-driven evolutionary program search.

entry.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
entry.summary:
FWL-ToPM and FWLAug introduce intensity-guided token reduction and physics-aware data augmentation to enable the first real-time, high-accuracy Transformer for Full-Waveform LiDAR.

Why it matters: It overcomes high computational costs and data scarcity in Full-Waveform LiDAR perception, enabling real-time deployment on autonomous vehicles operating in adverse environmental conditions.

entry.title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens
entry.summary:
Prepending trainable [DUMP] tokens to input sequences during contrastive embedding training reduces representational interference from low-information tokens without modifying model architecture, loss functions, or pooling strategies.

Why it matters: It offers a lightweight, architectural-change-free method to improve text embedding quality by isolating uninformative token noise during dense retrieval fine-tuning.

entry.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
StepX-OPD unifies multi-teacher capability consolidation and few-step distillation into a single stage, enabling diffusion models to learn multiple capabilities in a few steps while outperforming multi-step teachers.

Why it matters: It eliminates the performance degradation and GPU-hour overhead of sequential diffusion model compression by training fast, few-step models directly from specialized full-step teachers.

entry.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention
entry.summary:
Multi-layer Indexer (MLI) eliminates DeepSeek Sparse Attention's indexer bottleneck by running each layer's indexer concurrently with attention using the previous layer's selection, requiring no retraining, new weights, or extra kernels.

Why it matters: MLI significantly speeds up long-context LLM inference for architectures like DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 by overlapping indexer computation with attention, outperforming prior layer-dropping methods without degrading accuracy.

entry.title: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a model of costly competitive adjustment and a novel sandwich estimator to analyze how firms strategically reallocate capacity in response to cash flow shocks, validating it via vector-based representations of corporate news.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how dense vector representations generated by language models can be used to track corporate strategic adjustments and quantify competitive crowding in market ecosystems.

entry.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
entry.summary:
TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive streaming audio-video framework that uses a progressive-resolution multi-step trajectory, history-passing across chunks, and asymmetric text continuation training for high-resolution digital human generation.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, real-time, high-resolution digital human audio-video streaming without speech artifacts during dynamic text updates.

entry.title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
entry.summary:
KernelSeek uses question-driven prompts instead of complex tools or fixed scripts to optimize CUDA kernels, outperforming FlashAttention-3 and FlashAttention-4.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted, directional questioning is more effective for LLM-based GPU kernel optimization than equipping agents with heavy external toolsets and libraries.

entry.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a security vulnerability in offline RAG systems where signed precomputed vectors can be manipulated independently of text, and propose a deterministic code-verification method to restore text-vector integrity.

Why it matters: Accepting precomputed embeddings based on standard signatures or cosine tolerances allows malicious publishers to hijack RAG retrieval results on edge devices without altering the visible text.

entry.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
entry.summary:
An evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5 reveals zero-shot weight reading of small CNNs relies on local arithmetic and memorized dataset priors rather than actual weight-flow tracing.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that current LLM weight-space programming capabilities are driven by local arithmetic and dataset memorization rather than true internal weight-flow reasoning.

entry.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
entry.summary:
Circe is a training-free LLM self-evaluation method that assesses response correctness without reference answers by combining internal model interaction signals with external output confidence.

Why it matters: Circe enables reliable, training-free evaluation of LLM response correctness in real-world deployment settings where ground-truth reference answers are unavailable.

entry.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
entry.summary:
Strong-to-weak on-policy distillation using external post-trained teachers is less compute-efficient than GRPO, but distilling a student's own GRPO expert checkpoints achieves target accuracy with up to 50x fewer distillation FLOPs.

Why it matters: Using self-GRPO checkpoints and multi-teacher OPD drastically lowers the compute required to combine domain-specific expert capabilities into a single competitive model.

entry.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Analysis of LoRA dynamics reveals that group-mean baseline subtraction in RL concentrates singular spectra and accelerates subspace rotation compared to SFT, enabling tailored spectral-flattening interventions that improve performance in both stages.

Why it matters: Understanding the distinct mathematical dynamics between SFT and RL allows practitioners to optimize LoRA hyperparameters and update mechanisms specifically tailored for each tuning stage.

entry.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
entry.summary:
Muir enhances linear attention by introducing sensitivity-allocated low-rank gating, matched-filter state readout, and a numerically stable parallel update algorithm for large chunk sizes.

Why it matters: Muir enables scalable linear-attention models to achieve superior long-context retention and lower perplexity than Transformers while maintaining fast, constant-memory inference.

entry.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
entry.summary:
StrataFlux is an LLM inference framework that recovers accuracy lost in 2-4-bit weight and 2-3-bit KV-cache quantization by selectively streaming refinement precision from host RAM and SSDs without stalling generation.

Why it matters: It breaks the hardware memory ceiling for LLM inference, enabling low-bit quantized models to achieve high-precision accuracy levels using secondary host storage without suffering typical offloading latency penalties.

entry.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
FewStepRL adapts reinforcement learning post-training objectives to few-step diffusion models using a systematic three-phase framework consisting of transformation, decomposition, and adaptation.

Why it matters: It enables computationally efficient RL fine-tuning of diffusion models by overcoming the math mismatch between standard many-step RL objectives and few-step interval-velocity models.

entry.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
entry.summary:
SwarmEvolve accelerates program optimization by using hundreds of low-cost agents per round that reason and combine ideas directly in latent space via KV-cache passing.

Why it matters: Communicating through latent space rather than decoded text drastically cuts the compute time and cost required for LLM-driven evolutionary code discovery.

entry.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
entry.summary:
A survey of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety that introduces a unified framework for evaluating claims, synthesizes research methods, and provides hands-on open-source notebooks.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured taxonomy and evaluation framework to determine whether understanding internal model mechanics can reliably improve AI control, steering, and safety.

entry.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
entry.summary:
StepBack is a step-level test-time reasoning method that localizes the first error in draft trajectories using lightweight signals and resamples only from that error step forward.

Why it matters: It significantly cuts token generation costs and latency for chain-of-thought reasoning without sacrificing task accuracy.

entry.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
entry.summary:
Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM) improves agent decisions by combining a frozen language model semantic encoder with a shared, frozen conditional predictor (LimiX-2) that infers task targets from deployment evidence without parameter updates.

Why it matters: By decoupling semantic representation from empirical inference, DPDM allows LLM agents to continuously learn from deployment history and improve decision accuracy without costly model fine-tuning.

entry.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
entry.summary:
VFlash introduces Flash Primitive Decoding, a method using a lightweight drafter to predict structured visual primitives jointly in a single forward pass instead of token-by-token.

Why it matters: By drastically reducing generation latency while improving spatial accuracy, VFlash enables real-time visual goal and trajectory planning for physical AI systems like robotics and autonomous driving.

entry.title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
entry.summary:
Harness-S uses a fixed pool of specialized sibling harnesses to rescue failed policy attempts during training, distilling auxiliary execution capabilities into a single policy that executes under the original base harness.

Why it matters: It allows AI agents to internalize capabilities discovered through diverse, specialized execution environments without requiring complex or non-standard harnesses at deployment time.

entry.title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand
entry.summary:
BestRand is a benchmark compression method that mitigates random sampling's high-error tail while cutting subset construction costs and improving out-of-distribution estimation accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables stable, accurate, and cheap LLM and multimodal evaluation by preventing the rare, massive estimation errors inherent to basic random sampling.

entry.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
entry.summary:
WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model using a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture with sparse Mixture-of-Experts to integrate multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, editing, and multi-reference synthesis.

Why it matters: It enables high-resolution image generation, instruction editing, and multi-reference synthesis within a single unified model efficient enough for single-GPU consumer deployments.

entry.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
entry.summary:
TailSteer is a final-stage training framework that prevents multi-turn visual drift by concentrating preservation corrections at the tail of on-policy denoising trajectories.

Why it matters: It allows foundation image models to sustain robust multi-turn editing over long horizons without requiring expensive retraining or specialized inference-time mechanisms.

entry.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
entry.summary:
SLA is a Spatial-Language-Action model that integrates implicit spatial alignment into continual pre-training for VLAs using 3D perception supervision without adding inference overhead.

Why it matters: It establishes transferable 3D spatial understanding as a foundational capability in vision-language-action models while maintaining zero additional computational cost during deployment.

entry.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
entry.summary:
EvoMemState is a state-centric long-term memory framework for LLM agents that augments persistent facts with evolving Relational States and a request-specific Reasoning State trained via reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It improves retrieval completeness and response accuracy in long-term personal AI agents by explicitly modeling how facts conflict, relate, and apply to specific user requests over time.

entry.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
D3D is a standalone diffusion drafter that decouples candidate generation from target-model hidden states, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding by drafting successor blocks concurrently during target verification.

Why it matters: By eliminating sequential dependencies between drafting and target verification, D3D significantly increases inference throughput for large language models without degrading acceptance performance.

entry.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
entry.summary:
Drex is a family of four open decision models (up to 27B parameters) that output probability distributions over user-provided options in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding.

Why it matters: Decision models like Drex dramatically reduce latency and inference costs while providing consistent, non-autoregressive output formats for structured classification and scoring tasks.

entry.title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
VisSearch-Bench introduces 204 human-written tasks across 5 search categories to evaluate multimodal agents on long-horizon visual search and visual context management.

Why it matters: Current multimodal models struggle significantly with tasks requiring long-horizon reasoning that bridges visual evidence, spatial relations, and web search retrieval.

entry.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
entry.summary:
Hybrid Computer Use (HCU) is a unified interface for general agents that combines programmatic, accessibility-based semantic, and visual GUI interactions to improve execution efficiency and accuracy.

Why it matters: Enabling agents to flexibly combine programmatic, semantic, and visual modalities reduces round-trip latency and overcomes the performance bottlenecks of purely visual, human-centric GUI interfaces.

entry.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
entry.summary:
PLatour is an open-source framework connecting frozen language models via zero-initialized linear bridges for Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer, paired with PACT-Check to verify genuine communication gains.

Why it matters: It provides tools to efficiently combine large and small language models while offering a critical diagnostic method to prevent false attribution of performance gains to latent cross-model communication.

entry.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
entry.summary:
Open-HumanScale provides an open-source recipe and 50,000-hour curated egocentric video corpus (Open-HumanScale-50K) for pretraining embodied world-action models.

Why it matters: It establishes a reproducible, open-source framework and empirical scaling law for leveraging massive egocentric human video to improve physical robot generalization.

entry.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
entry.summary:
Researchers derived SIMPLE, a four-parameter analytical law that predicts LLM inference energy consumption across model architectures and NVIDIA H100 GPUs without per-LLM calibration.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, uncalibrated prediction of LLM inference energy costs, uncovering energy inefficiencies in long-context, agentic, and extended reasoning workloads.

entry.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) that use a label-free RL objective to generate text exemplars directly from language model residual stream directions, bypassing the limitations of corpus search.

Why it matters: MAEMs offer a grounded, scalable approach to mechanistically interpret internal model representations without relying on fixed external text corpora or manual labeling.

entry.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A new parallel decoding method for diffusion language models uses internal forward-pass probes to directly measure token coupling, improving decoding speed over standard mean-field decoding.

Why it matters: It enables faster inference and lower step counts for diffusion language models without requiring model retraining or architectural modifications.

entry.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
entry.summary:
Researchers established an analytical framework using high-dimensional invariant boxes to prove that the first token acts as an exponential attractor in deep Mamba models, driving token clustering and attention-sink behavior.

Why it matters: Proving that Mamba architecture inherently exhibits first-token attraction provides a mathematical foundation for understanding attention-sink phenomena and token clustering in state-space models.

entry.title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
entry.summary:
SpecCTMC is a training-free speculative sampler for masked diffusion language models that reduces sequential evaluations without a separate draft model while preserving the exact continuous-time Markov chain distribution.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster parallel text generation in diffusion language models while maintaining exact output distribution fidelity without requiring retraining or auxiliary draft models.

entry.title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
entry.summary:
Hybrid State Transfer (HST) enables cross-model state handoff in hybrid linear-attention LLMs by mapping full-attention K/V caches, recurrent states, and convolution histories to bypass prefill during model switches.

Why it matters: HST eliminates the overhead of repeating prefill over long contexts when routing or cascading between different sizes of hybrid linear-attention LLMs.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
A mechanistic framework analyzes how on-policy distillation's feedback loop causes limited student responsiveness and generation degeneration, while showing offline distillation can successfully prepare models for effective on-policy training.

Why it matters: Understanding OPD's feedback mechanics helps practitioners avoid training degeneration and effectively sequence offline preparation to unlock downstream performance gains in post-training.

entry.title: CoRD: Coupled Rollouts Fill the Blind Spot of On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
CoRD improves on-policy distillation by generating rollout states from a geometric interpolation of student and teacher models using maximal coupling from speculative decoding.

Why it matters: CoRD provides a more data-efficient sampling mechanism that exposes student models to critical teacher states without needing frequent or ad-hoc state interventions.

entry.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
entry.summary:
Researchers mapped masked diffusion parallel text generation to statistical physics and random sequential adsorption, deriving an exact solution for Markov data and a thermodynamic metric to calculate optimal unmasking schedules.

Why it matters: The theoretical framework enables the mathematical optimization of unmasking schedules to improve speed and output quality in parallel-decoded masked diffusion models.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers established scaling laws for sparse autoencoder (SAE) training data, demonstrating that replaying a fixed activation buffer after reaching a quality plateau achieves performance equivalent to using entirely fresh activations.

Why it matters: This approach significantly reduces activation storage requirements by up to 64x during SAE training, dramatically lowering memory bottlenecks and compute costs without sacrificing model interpretability or reconstruction quality.

entry.title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix
entry.summary:
Overlap-gated On-Policy Distillation (O²PD) restricts distillation to the first 20% prefix tokens of student rollouts and uses an overlap-gated α-divergence to address top-k alignment failure modes.

Why it matters: O²PD improves student model training efficiency and stability by filtering out unreliable off-policy teacher supervision and resolving support mismatches in top-k distillation.

entry.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
entry.summary:
NEO-VLA is an encoder-free vision-language-action framework that tokenizes images via patch convolutions, enabling a flow-matching action expert to access multi-depth visual representations.

Why it matters: Directly integrating visual feature computation into the action backbone provides better spatial details and increases control robustness across distribution shifts in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary:
FrontierPhysics is a benchmark featuring 56 expert-authored end-to-end tasks across nine physics domains to evaluate whether AI agents can conduct correct, publishable research from literature review to manuscript generation.

Why it matters: It establishes an end-to-end evaluation framework that highlights critical reasoning and intuition bottlenecks in AI agents attempting autonomous scientific discovery.

entry.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
entry.summary:
A study evaluates multi-turn agentic RL using Pass@(K,T), revealing performance depends on turn budgets, primarily aids error recovery rather than single-step decisions, and introduces BudgetMix RL to improve resilience across execution settings.

Why it matters: Understanding RL's reliance on interaction depth allows developers to optimize training regimes like BudgetMix RL, ensuring agents remain effective under strict inference-time turn constraints.

entry.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
entry.summary:
PyRUA-DataFarm replaces human teleoperators with an LLM coding agent that builds simulation environments and expert controllers from one calibration episode, using a video model to render real-ready policy training data.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for manual robot teleoperation and physical hardware during data collection, lowering the cost and increasing the visual robustness of real-world policy deployment.

entry.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
entry.summary:
EmoReward introduces a self-evolving training mechanism for emotional video generation RL that uses reflective reward gating and historical reward traces to adaptively calibrate multi-reward fusion weights between training runs.

Why it matters: It mitigates reward hacking and subjective aesthetic inconsistencies in video RL post-training by dynamically weighting emotional cues without needing manual reward engineering or continuous reward model fine-tuning.

entry.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
entry.summary:
StreamDuo pairs a trainable streaming commentator with a frozen research agent that retrieves game wiki entries in real-time to enable accurate commentary on unseen games.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a viable framework for streaming video LLMs to zero-shot adapt to novel visual domains without unlearning general timing or hallucinating domain-specific terminology.

entry.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
entry.summary:
Solv3R is a looped transformer architecture that uses an iteration-independent update operator to iteratively refine multi-view geometry estimates and integrate new image observations.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for separate task-specific models in 3D reconstruction by enabling scalable, iterative refinement and real-time frame streaming within a single transformer framework.

entry.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
entry.summary:
H2RB is a co-training framework that adapts pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies using unpaired human and robot demonstrations by bridging representation and action spaces.

Why it matters: H2RB enables scalable policy adaptation by leveraging easy-to-collect human demonstrations, significantly reducing the reliance on expensive target-robot data collection.

entry.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
entry.summary:
Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD) unifies score and flow matching via a learned critic, enabling VA-TDM to achieve state-of-the-art four-step image and video generation.

Why it matters: VA-TDM enables high-fidelity, few-step image and video generation on massive models, significantly reducing computational inference costs while retaining full-model quality.

entry.title: VideoMemBench: How Well Do MLLMs Remember in Video Conversations?
entry.summary:
VideoMemBench evaluates in-context video memory in MLLMs using multi-turn dialogues with cross-turn dependencies requiring models to recall prior visual contexts and their own past answers.

Why it matters: Current MLLMs fail to maintain context across multi-turn video conversations, highlighting a major limitation in deploying models for continuous interactive video analysis.

entry.title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens
entry.summary:
TAC-CoT is an adaptive implicit Chain-of-Thought framework that replaces explicit reasoning text with compact latent tokens while preserving textual tokens for tool calls, observations, and final answers.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to execute tool-assisted reasoning with significantly lower generation overhead without sacrificing accuracy or tool-use capabilities.

entry.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Muon-RT eliminates Muon's separate momentum buffer during self-distillation by reusing the teacher-student model displacement to compute orthogonalized update vectors with reduced training memory.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces persistent GPU memory overhead during LLM self-distillation while simultaneously outperforming both AdamW and standard Muon in model accuracy.

entry.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
SpecOPD accelerates speculative decoding drafter training using branch-parallel on-policy distillation, decoupling supervision from sequential rollouts while optimizing acceptance length directly via an E2E-TV surrogate.

Why it matters: It dramatically scales up on-policy distillation efficiency for speculative decoding drafters, yielding significant inference speedups across diverse model architectures up to 125B parameters.

entry.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
LoopVQ introduces a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that jointly codes multi-loop step channels and fine-tunes codebooks, achieving sub 1-bit quantization.

Why it matters: It eliminates the primary memory bottleneck in parameter-efficient looped transformers, enabling massive throughput gains and lower latency for long-context inference.

entry.title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World
entry.summary:
PyRUA-REAL is a framework for embodied recursive self-improvement that enables coding agents to transform real-world robot exploration into persistent memory and reusable executable code skills.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a method for robots to continuously improve their capabilities through physical interaction and convert that experience into efficient, reusable autonomous code.

entry.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
entry.summary:
Coca-Cola compresses LLM agent tool observations into continuous latent tokens instead of raw text, using Action-Preserving Training to maintain decision-critical information while drastically cutting context size and latency.

Why it matters: By bypassing text-based tool outputs in favor of continuous latent embeddings, multi-step LLM agents can run significantly faster and cheaper without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks
entry.summary:
A 36-expert study shows that model merging does not require uniform LoRA ranks across experts, provided the merge method avoids selecting spectral components purely by magnitude.

Why it matters: Practitioners can independently optimize the LoRA rank for each domain expert without degrading model performance during post-hoc merging.

entry.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
D3D introduces a standalone diffusion drafter combining blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding without waiting for target-model hidden states.

Why it matters: Eliminating the dependency on target-model hidden states allows overlapping execution of drafting and verification phases, significantly accelerating LLM inference speed.

entry.title: EvoOPD: Evolving Privileged Information Strategies for Black-Box On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
EvoOPD optimizes black-box language model distillation by dynamically evolving privileged information (PI) feedback strategies from the teacher based on the student model's changing state.

Why it matters: It enables effective fine-grained distillation from proprietary, logit-inaccessible language models by dynamically matching teacher feedback to the student's evolving learning needs.

entry.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
entry.summary:
Prompting LLMs with specific political personas systematically alters their latent space representational geometry, reorganizing word projections and semantic axis alignments.

Why it matters: Context-dependent reorganization of latent representations can undermine the reliability of standard LLM feature monitoring and safety evaluation tools like linear probes and sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models
entry.summary:
LooM introduces a causal encoder-decoder architecture that loops decoder layers using a loop-invariant key-value cache, enabling flexible dynamic depth without increasing memory usage.

Why it matters: LooM allows deployment-time compute scaling up to 21 layer executions per token without increasing memory footprint or requiring structural model changes.

entry.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse
entry.summary:
A study on non-prefix KV-cache reuse demonstrates that allocating a 5% repair budget to recomputing target chunks against reused context yields higher accuracy than re-inserting original prefill KV tensors or using InfoFlow reordering.

Why it matters: It establishes that limited computational repair budgets are best spent recomputing target chunks in place rather than restoring original prefill KV states or reordering context.

entry.title: Does Context Compression Preserve Refusal Alignment?
entry.summary:
Encoder-based context compression systematically weakens refusal alignment in instruction-tuned language models by attenuating activations along the decoder's refusal direction, despite high semantic reconstruction fidelity.

Why it matters: Systems using compressed context representations to save inference costs risk exposing safety vulnerabilities unless alignment-relevant features are explicitly preserved.

entry.title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
entry.summary:
Researchers developed an automated pipeline that combined LLM judges with evolutionary, RL, and subliminal learning methods to generate a dataset of 6,575 training datasets with surprising side effects across eight model behaviors.

Why it matters: Automating the discovery of unexpected training side effects provides a benchmark to study out-of-domain generalization and predict model misbehaviors prior to deployment.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary:
FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark comprising 56 expert-authored tasks designed to evaluate AI agents across complete physics research workflows.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous evaluation standard that shifts AI physics benchmarks from solving isolated static problems to assessing full-lifecycle research competence.
